questions.q: What happens on this capstone's pre-deployment checklist if even one ATF test in the Critical Path suite fails or is skipped?
options: It is treated as a hard stop with no exceptions, regardless of how minor the failure seems
The deployment proceeds anyway as long as most tests passed
Only the server-side test matters, so a failing UI Test can be ignored
The checklist item is simply removed for that deployment
questions.explain: The runbook treats a failing or skipped test as a full stop — "it's probably fine" is explicitly ruled out.

questions.q: Why does the pre-deployment checklist specifically call out dependency sequencing, referencing Chapter 2?
options: Because a new field must commit before a Flow Action that reads it, in every instance the change promotes through, or it risks the kind of collision Chapter 2 covered
Because dependency order never matters once ATF tests are passing
Because Chapter 2 only applies to the Dev instance
Because Update Sets are no longer used once Source Control is connected
questions.explain: Getting the sequence wrong — promoting a dependent component before what it depends on — is exactly the kind of Update Set collision Chapter 2 addressed.

questions.q: How does this capstone's rollback mechanism actually revert a bad production deployment?
options: By reverting the Git commit and re-promoting the prior known-good version through the same Dev to Test to Prod pipeline
By hand-editing the Prod instance directly to undo the change
By deleting the scoped application entirely and starting over
Rollback is not possible once a change reaches Prod
questions.explain: Because the application is Source Control-connected, rollback goes back through the same pipeline rather than hand-editing Prod, which the course treats as an anti-pattern from Chapter 1 onward.

questions.q: What is the specific, predefined trigger condition for starting rollback immediately in this runbook?
options: A failed ATF Suite re-run against Prod within the first hour, or confirmed student reports of being unable to register for open sections
Waiting 48 hours to see if anyone complains before deciding
Any deployment that occurs outside of business hours
A trigger condition is deliberately left undefined so the team can decide in the moment
questions.explain: The runbook defines the trigger in advance specifically so nobody is improvising a judgment call under pressure.

questions.q: Why could the Course Registration application still fail in production even after passing every ATF test and following this exact deployment runbook?
options: Because ATF testing confirmed correctness, not behavior under real production load, which is exactly what the next course, ServiceNow Performance Troubleshooting, addresses
Because ATF tests are purely cosmetic and never actually verify real behavior
Because the deployment runbook in this lesson is incomplete and missing basic steps
Because Change Management approval guarantees performance under load
questions.explain: Correctness tests never simulated thousands of students hitting the form in the same window — that load-related gap is precisely where course 12 picks up.
